description: Grupo de Oficiales Becarios de la FAE en la UFA-ESPE.
summary: We created an interactive storytelling platform that brings Mars exploration to Earth by using real planetary analogs. We tackled this challenge by integrating NASA Earth observation datasets with orbital data from Mars and the Moon to pinpoint terrestrial environments that share critical similarities in topography, climate (temperature and lighting), and physical processes—such as erosion, permafrost, and the presence of extremophiles. These metrics power an immersive experience where users make decisions based on real-world scenarios. Its impact lies in turning complex scientific data into accessible simulations, helping build decision-making skills for future crewed missions while sparking educational and scientific interest in astrobiology and space exploration right from our own planet.
details: We developed a data-driven, immersive interactive narrative that simulates Martian scenarios using real planetary analogs on Earth. To tackle this challenge, we cross-referenced satellite data from NASA’s Global Earth Observation Datasets with planetary records from Mars and the Moon. This analysis pinpoints terrestrial regions that replicate key Martian conditions across three core pillars: geology (topography), environment (temperature and lighting), and physical processes (water, ice, permafrost, erosion, and extremophiles). Based on this data, we built a sensory experience where users face and solve real-world space exploration challenges. This project matters because it democratizes planetary science—mentally and technically preparing people for the challenges of future Mars missions, while turning complex scientific data into an accessible educational tool that sparks curiosity and research into worlds beyond our own. On the technical side, we used Google Earth Engine to power the interactive map and Gemini AI to generate the code needed to integrate NASA’s datasets into it, alongside React, Vercel, Google Flow, ChatGPT (Astra), and Claude (Sonnet)—all brought together with natural-sounding voiceovers and an original script.
